title: Spread complexity as a probe in generalized and long-range Aubry-Andre-Harper models
authors: Triyas Sapui, Tanoy Kanti Konar, Subinay Dasgupta, Aditi Sen De
abstract: We investigate the spread complexity of quantum quenches in generalized and long-range Aubry-Andre-Harper (AAH) models, encompassing regimes with and without mobility edges. In particular, in the generalized AAH models supporting energy-dependent mobility edges, we demonstrate that the long-time averaged spread complexity exhibits nonanalytic behavior when the post-quench quasiperiodic potential crosses the mobility edge associated with the energy of the initial eigenstate, thereby accurately identifying the mobility-edge transition. Such a behavior is supported by the spreading of local density of states. We further derive analytical expressions for the moments and the corresponding Lanczos coefficients for quenches between the limits of vanishing and strong quasiperiodic potentials. The Lanczos coefficients display qualitatively distinct behavior depending on the presence of mobility edges - they exhibit an initial plateau followed by a decay with the Krylov basis index, in contrast to the nearly constant behavior of the conventional AAH model without mobility edges. For LR hopping, the coefficients decay with the Krylov basis index for quenches from the localized to the extended phase, while they coincide with the AAH results for quenches in the opposite direction.
summary: The paper uses spread complexity as a powerful diagnostic tool to study localization-delocalization transitions in generalized Aubry-André-Harper models. By analyzing how this complexity changes during quantum quenches across different potential regimes, the authors accurately pinpoint mobility edges. This methodology provides deep insights into the underlying single-particle dynamics of quasiperiodic systems.
main_problem: The study investigates spread complexity as a dynamical probe to characterize quantum phase transitions, particularly identifying mobility edges in quasiperiodic systems.
main_result: Nonanalytic behavior in the long-time averaged spread complexity accurately identifies the mobility-edge transition in generalized AAH models. The Lanczos coefficients also show distinct signatures depending on the presence of such mobility edges.
method: The analysis employs time evolution simulations using the Lanczos algorithm to construct a Krylov basis and calculate the long-time averaged spread complexity, alongside analyzing Lanczos coefficients and IPR.
model_or_system: The primary model is the generalized and long-range Aubry-André-Harper (AAH) model, which describes localization phenomena due to competition between hopping and a quasiperiodic onsite potential. The Hamiltonian includes terms for long-range hopping ($\alpha$) and an energy-dependent potential deformation ($ eta$).
key_observables: Spread complexity ($C$), Lanczos coefficients ($\{a_n, b_n\}$), Inverse Participation Ratio (IPR), and moments of the survival amplitude.
important_parameters: The quasiperiodicity strength ($\lambda'$), the long-range hopping exponent ($\alpha$), and the potential deformation parameter ($ eta$) are key parameters controlling different physical regimes.
main_assumptions: The analysis focuses on single-particle systems, which is noted as a gap compared to studies in interacting many-body systems. Calculations rely on taking limits (e.g., thermodynamic limit $N 	o \infty$).
figures_summary: Figures compare IPR and spread complexity ($C$) across different AAH model parameters ($\lambda$), demonstrating phase boundary detection. They also show comparisons of Lanczos coefficients for forward and backward quenches across various hopping ranges (NN, NNN, LR).
paper_structure: The paper develops the theoretical framework by defining spread complexity and applying it to generalized AAH models undergoing quantum quenches. It presents analytical derivations for moments and then compares the diagnostic power of $C$ against established methods like IPR across different hopping regimes (short-range vs. long-range).
why_interesting: This work provides a sophisticated, quantifiable dynamical tool (spread complexity) to map out phase diagrams in quasiperiodic systems, complementing traditional spectral measures like IPR and offering insights into the underlying quantum dynamics near critical points.
